title: It Was a Record-Breaking Year for Dust Storms
gist: The World Meteorological Organization's July 2026 Dust Bulletin, covering 2025, reports global dust surface concentrations comparable to 2024 but record-breaking dust and sand storm impacts in specific regions — including storms across Oklahoma and Texas on March 14, 2025, described as the worst since the Dust Bowl in some places. The signal is regional concentration hidden inside a flat global average.

insights.claim: The World Meteorological Organization publishes an annual Dust Bulletin recording how many sand and dust storms hit the planet over a 12-month period and how dangerous they are for air quality, health and the environment.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: A recurring, standardized global dataset to monitor for regional air-quality and agricultural disruption risk.
insights.quote: Every year the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) puts out a Dust Bulletin—a record of how many sand and dust storms hit our planet over a 12-month period
insights.locator: Every year the World Meteorological Organization

insights.claim: The July 2026 Dust Bulletin covers calendar year 2025 and found overall dust surface concentrations comparable to 2024, showing no deterioration in the global aggregate.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Global-average dust is flat year over year, so headlines about a record dust year are about distribution, not total load.
insights.quote: while the overall dust surface concentrations were comparable to 2024
insights.locator: The July 2026 bulletin has now arrived

insights.claim: Despite flat global dust concentrations in 2025, certain areas were significantly impacted by dust and sand storms to a record-breaking level, meaning the hazard is regionally concentrated rather than globally distributed.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Model dust risk at the regional asset level — global averages will systematically understate localized crop, logistics and health exposure.
insights.quote: there were certain areas that were significantly impacted by dust and sand storms—to a record-breaking level, in some cases
insights.locator: The July 2026 bulletin has now arrived

insights.claim: Dust storms swept across Oklahoma and Texas on March 14, 2025, an event severe enough to be characterized as the worst since the Dust Bowl in some places.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: A Dust Bowl-scale comparison in the US southern plains is a flag for agricultural yield, insurance and regional air-quality exposure.
